cf.title: pg_dump: Fetch sequence data only for sequences being dumped

input.subject: BUG #19688: pg_dump --schema scans all sequences in PostgreSQL 18, causing severe performance regression

verdict_reasoning: The problem is stated with numbers and the demand is a field report of a v18 regression, so levels 1a and 1b pass. One fixable design objection survived, prior-attempts-1: the thread does not show that the OID list covers every sequence whose value pg_dump emits under binary upgrade, extension configuration or --data-only with filters. That is a coverage question for someone who knows pg_dump, and it does not put the idea in doubt.

brief.title: pg_dump: read sequence data only for sequences being dumped
brief.problem: Since commit bd15b7db48 (v18), pg_dump calls pg_get_sequence_data() for every sequence in the database, even for a dump limited by --schema or --table. Users with many sequences, such as schema-per-tenant databases, see selective dumps become much slower than in v16. Such a dump can also block on a lock held on a sequence it does not dump.
brief.proposed_design: collectSequences() passes the OIDs of the sequences whose data will be dumped to its query, and calls pg_get_sequence_data() only for those. Definitions are still fetched for all sequences from pg_sequence, a catalog scan. The author offers versions for HEAD, REL_19_STABLE and REL_18_STABLE.
author_claims: The reporter saw a schema dump go from about 50 seconds on v16 to about 5.5 minutes on 18.6, with 142237 sequences in the database and 329 in the schema.
With the reporter's own patch, the same dump took about 50 seconds again, with identical TOC, SQL output and restored sequence state.
On HEAD with 20000 sequences in one schema and 4 in another, "pg_dump -n small" dropped from about 1.3 s to 0.33 s.
A selective dump no longer waits on an AccessExclusiveLock held on an unrelated sequence, such as an uncommitted DROP SEQUENCE.
The fix is a v18 regression fix and should be backpatched through 18; tests and output comparisons pass on all branches.
brief.thread_state: Two messages on pgsql-bugs: the bug report with a proof-of-concept patch, and Andrew Krylosov's reply with v1 patches for three branches. No committer or reviewer has replied in the thread, though three reviewers are listed in the CommitFest entry.
unclear: The material does not say how the patch builds the OID list, or whether a very long OID array in the query string causes problems for large partial dumps.
It does not say whether full dumps keep the existing bulk query or also use the OID list.
It does not say whether any test was added for selective dumps or for the lock wait case.
It does not say how sequences dumped only for data (for example --data-only with filters) or owned by extensions are handled.
It does not say whether the reporter's patch, which also restricted definitions, was compared with this one.
search_queries: pg_dump selective dump lock unrelated tables

prior_attempts.title: Ignore attributes of tables part of extensions in pg_dump
prior_attempts.quote: Hm. I have been pondering about this code more and I am dropping the patch as either adding a check based on the flag to track dumpable objects or ext_member visibly breaks the logic that binary upgrade and tables in extensions rely on.
prior_attempts.reason: The author withdrew the patch. A reviewer asked why it checked ext_member rather than the usual dobj.dump flag. The author concluded that skipping attributes based on either flag would break binary upgrade, which still dumps extension member tables individually.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P7 skipped column fetching for extension member tables. This patch limits pg_get_sequence_data() calls to sequences whose data is dumped and keeps fetching definitions for all sequences.

objections.title: Data-OID filter may miss sequences dumped through binary upgrade or extensions
objections.failure_scenario: A user runs pg_upgrade, or dumps an extension whose configuration sequence is marked with pg_extension_config_dump. If the OID list misses a sequence whose value pg_dump still emits, the restore writes a wrong or default last_value. The next inserts then fail with duplicate keys, possibly weeks after the upgrade.
objections.argument: [P7] was dropped because filtering a catalog fetch on pg_dump's dump flags "visibly breaks the logic that binary upgrade and tables in extensions rely on". This patch also filters a bulk fetch, here by which sequences have data dumped. Message #2 and the commit message do not cover binary upgrade, extension member sequences, or --data-only with filters. The reporter's tests in message #1 cover one --schema dump.
objections.author_must_show: For binary-upgrade dumps, extension configuration sequences and --data-only with filters, is every sequence whose value pg_dump emits in the OID list, and which test shows it?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows pg_dump's object selection, binary-upgrade mode and the sequence data collection added by commit bd15b7db48.
committability.liability: A backpatched change to pg_dump in 18, 19 and HEAD. If the OID list misses a sequence, a restore or pg_upgrade writes a wrong sequence value, and the error may appear long after.
committability.author_follow_up: The author supplied versions for three branches and created the CommitFest entry. The thread shows no later reply from the author.

priority.reason: Message #1 reports a schema dump going from about 50 seconds to about 5.5 minutes on a schema-per-tenant database. The patch touches one function in pg_dump.c and adds no user-visible surface.

provisional_note: The code was not read. How the patch builds the OID list, and whether it covers binary-upgrade, extension member and identity sequences, could not be checked.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump: optimize dumpFunc()
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace pg_dump's per-function query in dumpFunc() with a single query that gathers data for all functions up front, keeping the PGresult in memory and using a sorted array of function OIDs to locate each function's row. The aim was to reduce dump time for databases with many functions (shown as about 0.25s to about 0.11s for 10k simple functions).
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane questioned whether the change helps databases with few functions and what it does to pg_dump's memory requirements when there are very many functions with large source text, and said the shown results did not justify the risk. The author agreed and withdrew the patch.
matched_queries: pg_dump selective dump lock unrelated tables
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not sure that the results you're showing justify taking any
risk here.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve pg_dump dumping publication tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes pg_dump's getPublicationTables() to fetch all publication-table memberships with a single query, instead of iterating over every table and issuing a separate query per table. The matching TableInfo for each row is then looked up in tblinfoindex, which should be faster when there are many tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was superseded, not rejected: Tom Lane had already committed practically the same change in passing (commit 8e396a773), which also removed the server-side join. He therefore marked the entry withdrawn. Cary Huang's earlier concern about client-side memory use with very many publication tables was answered by Tom Lane as not significant compared to the per-table data pg_dump already collects.
matched_queries: pg_dump selective dump lock unrelated tables
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'll mark this CF entry "withdrawn", since it wasn't rejected
exactly.  Too bad we don't have a classification of "superseded
by events", or something like that.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump --where option
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a --where option to pg_dump that exposes pg_dump's existing internal ability to filter dumped table data with a WHERE clause, building on an earlier patch. This version aims to give clearer error messages for invalid clauses and to apply a filter only to a specified table instead of to every table matched by a pattern.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Daniel Gustafsson's review raised open issues: pasting arbitrary SQL into the query without schema-qualification checks may expose CVE-2018-1058-style problems, the patch had no tests, and it was unclear how quoted multibyte table names or table names containing colons would be handled. The author did not answer this review for two weeks, and Michael Paquier, noting that tests are needed, marked the entry returned with feedback.
matched_queries: pg_dump selective dump lock unrelated tables
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Documenting something is well and good, but isn't allowing arbitrary SQL
copy-pasted into the query (which isn't checked for schema qualification)
opening up for some of the ill-effects of CVE-2018-1058?

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump new feature: exporting functions only
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a pg_dump switch (--functions-only) to dump only stored functions and procedures from a database, without resolving their dependencies on other objects. During the discussion the design moved toward pattern-based include/exclude options per object type (e.g. --routine/--exclude-routine alongside --table, --schema, --extension).
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for a different design: pattern-matching options per object type with matching exclude options, in line with --table and --extension, instead of an all-or-nothing --functions-only switch. The author summarised the new plan and said she would rewrite the patch, but no reworked patch is shown before the deadline. The committer closing the entry concluded that a different design was wanted and that it would not make v15.
matched_queries: pg_dump selective dump lock unrelated tables
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Looks clear to me that a different design is wanted here, and that
this won't make it for v15, so I have marked the patch as returned
with feedback in the CF app.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump -C Grant statement on create database
precedents_retrieved.summary: When pg_dump is run with -C (emit CREATE DATABASE), it would also emit the database-level GRANT statements (such as GRANT CREATE ON DATABASE), matching what pg_dumpall already produces. The patch makes emitting these grants subject to the existing -x (no privileges) option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The thread contains only the original report, a reply agreeing it is an oversight, and the patch submission; no review or objection to the patch appears, and the entry was returned with feedback about three months later.
matched_queries: pg_dump selective dump lock unrelated tables

precedents_retrieved.title: Add --include-table-data-where option to pg_dump, to export only a subset of table data
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a pg_dump option (initially --include-table-data-where=table:filter_clause, later discussed as --where) that applies a user-supplied WHERE clause to the data dump of tables matching a pattern, so that only a subset of rows is exported. The option could be given multiple times, and each filter applied to every table matching its pattern.
precedents_retrieved.objection: It was returned with feedback because the patch had merge conflicts and was not rebased after a reviewer asked for it; the author posted a rebased patch only after the entry had been closed. Reviewers had also raised open design points about the option syntax: the use of a colon to separate table from clause, how colons in table or column names would be parsed, and how the option interacts with --table. One participant also questioned whether the feature was needed, given psql \copy.
matched_queries: pg_dump selective dump lock unrelated tables
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Given this patch has not been updated, I'm marking this as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Ignore attributes of tables part of extensions in pg_dump
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change pg_dump so that getTableAttrs skips fetching column and type information for tables that are members of an extension, using the ext_member flag. The goal was to avoid gathering attributes for tables that pg_dump does not dump individually.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch. A reviewer asked why it checked ext_member rather than the usual dobj.dump flag. The author concluded that skipping attributes based on either flag would break binary upgrade, which still dumps extension member tables individually.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent proposed the same fix. [P1] went the other way, toward a bulk query, and its 'results do not justify the risk' reason does not fit a measured v18 regression. Message #2 reports that the problem was first noted in the bug #19365 discussion; the thread gives no rejection reason from it.

The patch changes no syntax, option, GUC, psql behaviour or dump format, and the reporter found identical TOC, SQL output and restored sequence state, so the user-facing contract is unchanged. One point needs the code to check: whether every sequence whose data is dumped, such as identity sequences, extension configuration sequences, or sequences in --data-only and binary-upgrade runs, is already marked when collectSequences() builds its OID list.

The patch changes only which rows pg_dump's own catalog query returns. It has no on-disk format, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or server ABI change, and server state on primaries and standbys is untouched. One point cannot be checked without the code: under --binary-upgrade, which pg_upgrade uses, every sequence that needs its last_value must still be in the OID list, given the extension-member issue recorded in [P7].

The proposal has no new privilege or exposure aspect. It narrows which sequences pg_dump reads and locks, so a selective dump touches fewer objects and no longer waits on locks held on sequences it does not dump. It adds no new role, function, setting or visible output, so users can do or see nothing new.

From the maintenance angle this is a narrow fix to a v18 regression, confined to collectSequences() in pg_dump.c, with no new GUC, catalog, syntax or extension API. Restricting the query to an OID array copies how pg_dump already batches per-object queries, and full dumps lose nothing. Neither precedent applies: [P7] skipped data that binary upgrade needed, and [P1] traded memory for little gain, while this patch reduces work. Points that cannot be checked without the code: how the OID array behaves when a dump excludes one small schema and keeps over 100000 sequences, whether binary-upgrade and extension-member sequences still get their data rows, and whether a test covers selective dumps.

No existing feature does this job. Postgres has no pg_dump option, GUC or extension that skips pg_get_sequence_data() for sequences outside a --schema or --table dump, and the user cannot work around it without patching pg_dump. The patch fixes a v18 regression inside the existing mechanism and adds no second mechanism.

The material shows real demand: a field report with numbers (142237 sequences, a schema dump going from about 50 seconds to about 5.5 minutes) on a common schema-per-tenant design, with daily per-schema backups no longer fitting in a day. This is a v18 regression with no user-visible surface, and its cost falls on nobody else.
